preamble: Depalatalization of [pʲ] to plain [p] removes the palatal secondary articulation of a labial stop. Palatalized labials are perceptually weak in coda position, where the palatal release has no following vowel to carry it, and Polish, Ukrainian and Belarusian hardened word-final soft labials. In Polish the change took place in the late 16th century and the old softness survives only before vowel-initial endings (karp, gen. karpia 'carp'); Ukrainian likewise has no palatalized labials word-finally (степ vs Russian степь 'steppe').

examples.from: older soft-stem karp' [karpʲ] 'carp' (softness kept in gen. karpia)
examples.note: Word-final soft labials lost their palatalization in the late 16th century; the soft stem survives in the oblique cases (karpia), as in gołąb, gen. gołębia 'pigeon'.
Ukrainian and Belarusian hardened all word-final soft labials (compare Russian степь [sʲtʲepʲ], which keeps the palatalization); the Ukrainian genitive степу is hard as well.
